objectives: Explain why attention needs position information
Compare sinusoidal vs learned vs rotary encodings

slides.title: Part 1 — Why position must be injected
slides.body: Self-attention is astonishingly powerful and has exactly one blind spot. Patch it correctly and you understand why every position-encoding scheme since 2017 looks the way it does.

slides.title: Self-attention is permutation-equivariant
slides.body: Stripped of position info, self-attention treats its input as a **set**, not a sequence. Permute the input tokens by any permutation $\pi$ and the outputs permute by the *same* $\pi$ — the function commutes with reordering. Proof sketch: $Q,K,V$ are row-wise projections (a permutation of rows permutes them identically), $QK^{T}$ permutes rows and columns, softmax is row-wise, and $AV$ follows — net effect is exactly the input permutation. Consequence: with no position signal, "dog bites man" and "man bites dog" produce the *same multiset* of outputs. Word order — which carries much of natural-language meaning — is invisible. This is not a bug to fix in attention; it's a property to *complement*.

slides.title: The fix: add a position-dependent vector
slides.body: Before the first attention layer, add a vector $PE(\text{pos})\in\mathbb{R}^{d}$ to each token embedding: $\tilde{x}_i = x_i + PE(i)$. Now two copies of the same word at different positions have *different* representations, so $Q/K$ derived from them differ, so attention *can* condition on order. The symmetry is broken deliberately and minimally — content still lives in $x_i$, position rides alongside. Every scheme (sinusoidal, learned, RoPE, ALiBi) is a different answer to one question: *what should the position signal be, and where should it enter?*

slides.title: Sinusoidal — the original recipe (and its cleverness)
slides.body: $PE_{(pos,2i)}=\sin\!\big(pos/10000^{2i/d}\big)$, $PE_{(pos,2i+1)}=\cos(\cdot)$. Two designed properties: (1) **uniqueness** — each position gets a distinct multi-frequency fingerprint (low dims oscillate fast = fine position, high dims slow = coarse position), so no two positions collide; (2) **linear relative offsets** — because $\sin(a{+}b),\cos(a{+}b)$ are linear combinations of $\sin a,\cos a,\sin b,\cos b$, the encoding of position $pos{+}k$ is a *fixed linear function* of the encoding of $pos$ (independent of $pos$). So a head can learn "attend 3 tokens back" as a single linear map that works everywhere — relative position for free, and it extrapolates to lengths unseen in training.

question.explanation: Low dims oscillate fast (local position), high dims slowly (global position) — together a unique, relative-offset-friendly code.

question.question: Why does attention need positional encoding at all?
options: Attention is permutation-invariant — it sees every token pair but not their order
Attention cannot compute dot products without it
It is required for softmax to converge
question.explanation: Attention treats the input as a set: permuting inputs permutes outputs but doesn't change the computation. Order has to be injected into the inputs (added vectors) or into Q/K (RoPE) so the model can reason about sequence.

slides.title: Rotate, don't add
slides.body: Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) injects position by **rotating** the Q and K vectors (in 2-D coordinate pairs) by an angle proportional to position, *before* the dot product — rather than adding a vector to the embedding. The algebra then makes $Q_i\!\cdot\!K_j$ depend on the **relative** offset $i-j$ exactly, not on absolute $i,j$. Benefits that made it the default (Llama, GPT-NeoX, most 2023+ models): relative-position structure is built into the *attention score itself*, it composes cleanly with the KV-cache, and it extrapolates / can be interpolated to context lengths far beyond training (the basis of long-context fine-tuning).

slides.title: Why relative position is the right inductive bias
slides.body: Linguistic rules are overwhelmingly *relative*: "an adjective modifies the following noun", "a verb agrees with its subject a few tokens back". None of these depend on whether the phrase sits at absolute position 5 or 5,000. Encodings that make *relative* offset the natural variable (sinusoidal's linear property, RoPE's rotation, ALiBi's distance penalty) generalize across positions and lengths. Purely *learned absolute* embeddings (a trainable table indexed by position) overfit to positions seen in training and fail hard past the trained context window — the empirical reason the field moved away from them.

question.question: The main practical advantage of RoPE over learned absolute positional embeddings is:
options: It encodes RELATIVE position into Q·K and extrapolates to longer contexts than seen at training
It uses fewer parameters and is faster
It removes the need to train the model
question.explanation: Learned absolute embeddings memorize only the positions seen in training — position 8000 is undefined if you trained to 4000. RoPE's rotation is parametric in position and shows up as a relative offset in the dot product, so it generalizes far better to long context.

slides.title: Part 4 — Ablate it and watch it break
No PE → an order-blind model (selective failure)
slides.body: Remove positional encoding entirely and the failure is *diagnostic precisely because it's selective*: order-agnostic tasks (topic classification, bag-of-words sentiment) still work passably, while anything order-dependent — "is X before Y?", subject vs object, syntax — collapses, because the model literally cannot distinguish token orderings (permutation equivariance). Seeing *which* capabilities survive tells you the cause is missing position info, not a broken layer. This selective-failure reasoning is a transferable debugging skill.

question.question: Order these positional schemes from OLDEST to NEWEST as the dominant default in transformer LLMs.
question.explanation: Sinusoidal came with the original 2017 transformer; learned absolute embeddings dominated the BERT/GPT-2 era; RoPE is the current default for modern LLMs because of its relative-position structure and extrapolation. (ALiBi is another modern relative-bias alternative.)

slides.title: What to carry forward
slides.body: Attention is permutation-equivariant; order is injected — added sinusoids (unique + linear-relative), or rotated in via RoPE (the modern default, relative-by-construction, length-extrapolating). Next: the per-token compute engine that holds most of the parameters — the **FFN**.
